presentation.name: Airflow DAG conventions
presentation.summary: Structures Airflow DAGs so nothing expensive or fragile runs at import time.
benefits: Keeps connections and queries out of module scope, where the scheduler re-runs them
Applies consistent default_args, retries and scheduling across DAGs
Flags import-time work that makes the scheduler slow or unstable

presentation.name: Change review
presentation.summary: Reviews a code change for correctness, risk, test coverage and backward compatibility.
benefits: Establishes what the change is supposed to do before judging whether it does it
Separates blocking defects from preferences, so findings are actionable
Checks backward compatibility for callers the diff does not show
Reports unverified areas instead of implying the whole change was checked

presentation.name: Data incident investigation
presentation.summary: Traces wrong data back to the code that produced it when the pipeline reported success.
benefits: Keeps the investigation read-only until a cause is proven
Turns symptoms into hypotheses a single query can rule out
Records evidence and unproven gaps in a written incident log

presentation.name: dbt error debugging
presentation.summary: Diagnoses a failing dbt build from the compiled SQL rather than the error text.
benefits: Reads the compiled SQL, where the real error usually is
Checks upstream models before blaming the failing one
Says when to stop patching symptoms and fix the source

presentation.name: dbt incremental models
presentation.summary: Chooses an incremental strategy and unique key that survive late data and schema drift.
benefits: Matches the strategy to how the source actually changes
Handles late-arriving rows instead of silently dropping them
Detects divergence between incremental and full-refresh output

presentation.name: dbt model creation
presentation.summary: Runs the build-and-verify loop for a new dbt model instead of stopping at compile.
benefits: Reads the project's existing layering and naming before writing
Builds and inspects real output rather than only compiling
Checks grain and row counts before the model is called done

presentation.name: dbt model documentation
presentation.summary: Writes model and column descriptions that state what the SQL cannot.
benefits: Puts the model's grain first, so consumers know what a row is
Records business rules, units and timezones that are invisible in the data
Skips filler descriptions that only restate the column name

presentation.name: dbt model refactoring
presentation.summary: Restructures a dbt model while proving its output did not change.
benefits: Finds the full downstream blast radius from the dbt graph, not grep
Captures the current output before any edit
Separates safe internal changes from interface changes that break consumers

presentation.name: dbt model testing
presentation.summary: Picks dbt schema tests that catch real defects for each column role.
benefits: Chooses tests by what the column is, not by habit
Covers keys, relationships and accepted values where they matter
Gives a procedure for what to do when a test fails

presentation.name: dbt project conventions
presentation.summary: Establishes what belongs in each dbt layer and why the boundaries hold.
benefits: Places sources, staging, intermediate and mart logic consistently
Applies contracts and tests at the layer where they are meaningful
Prevents business logic leaking into the staging layer

presentation.name: Legacy SQL to dbt
presentation.summary: Ports legacy SQL into dbt layer by layer and reconciles against the original.
benefits: Separates what to reuse from what to rewrite
Builds the staging layer before porting business logic
Reconciles migrated output against the legacy result

presentation.name: Error diagnosis
presentation.summary: Finds the cause of a failure by narrowing it down and proving it before changing code.
benefits: Establishes a reliable reproduction before theorising about causes
Turns guesses into hypotheses that a single observation can rule out
Confirms the cause explains every symptom, not just the loudest one
Stops speculative edits that hide a defect instead of fixing it

presentation.name: ETL decomposition
presentation.summary: Splits a monolithic extract-transform-load function into testable units with I/O at the edges.
benefits: Isolates the transform so it can be tested without network or database
Puts fetch and write behind thin I/O modules
Says when a function is small enough to leave alone

presentation.name: Implementation planning
presentation.summary: Turns agreed requirements into an ordered plan with verifiable steps.
benefits: Breaks work into steps that can each be checked independently
Orders steps so the riskiest assumption is tested early
States done criteria per step, not just for the whole task
Names what the plan does not cover, instead of implying full scope

presentation.name: Pipeline output review
presentation.summary: Reviews the data a pipeline run actually produced, not just whether tests passed.
benefits: Reconciles row accounting so silently dropped rows surface
Checks keys, contracts and drift against a recorded baseline
Reports INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE instead of guessing a verdict

presentation.name: Pipeline regression gates
presentation.summary: Selects the cheapest checks that would actually catch the regression a change can cause.
benefits: Maps the type of change to the layers of testing it requires
Avoids full end-to-end runs for defects a unit test would catch
Records which layers were skipped rather than implying full coverage

presentation.name: Plan execution
presentation.summary: Works through an agreed plan one step at a time and handles it when reality diverges.
benefits: Keeps each step small enough to verify before the next one starts
Gives a rule for when to adapt the plan and when to stop and ask
Prevents unrequested scope from being added mid-execution
Keeps the plan and the actual state of the work in agreement

presentation.name: Project documentation
presentation.summary: Documents architecture decisions, component boundaries and constraints a reader cannot infer from the code.
benefits: Records why a decision was made, not just what the code does
Makes component boundaries and their contracts explicit
Captures non-obvious constraints before they are rediscovered the hard way
Keeps documentation updated in the same change that invalidates it

presentation.name: pytest for data pipelines
presentation.summary: Tests data pipeline code with pytest, mocking at the I/O boundary.
benefits: Draws a clear unit and integration split for pipeline code
Mocks at the I/O edge so transforms stay genuinely tested
Adds DAG import tests that catch breakage before deployment

presentation.name: Refactoring safety
presentation.summary: Plans and sequences a refactor so behaviour is provably unchanged at every step.
benefits: Establishes a behavioural baseline before the first edit
Separates internal restructuring from interface changes that break callers
Sequences the work so each step can be verified and reverted alone
Says when a refactor should stop rather than expand

presentation.name: Requirements brainstorming
presentation.summary: Works out what is actually needed before any code is written.
benefits: Surfaces the real goal behind a requested solution
Separates stated requirements from assumptions that were never confirmed
Makes constraints and non-goals explicit before design starts
Says when enough is known to begin, so discovery does not run forever

presentation.name: SCD Type 2 implementation
presentation.summary: Implements Slowly Changing Dimension Type 2 in SQL with correct validity intervals.
benefits: Builds non-overlapping validity intervals with exactly one current row
Detects real attribute changes instead of rewriting history on every load
Avoids the idempotency traps that duplicate rows on re-run

presentation.name: Snowflake cost hunting
presentation.summary: Finds the Snowflake queries actually worth optimising and reads the metrics that point at a fix.
benefits: Picks the right history view for the question being asked
Ranks by credits rather than elapsed time when cost is the concern
Turns query metrics into a specific next action

presentation.name: Snowflake query diagnosis
presentation.summary: Diagnoses one Snowflake query from its profile and operator statistics.
benefits: Reads pruning and spill statistics to locate the real bottleneck
Separates a query problem from a warehouse sizing problem
Points at the specific operator responsible for the cost

presentation.name: Snowflake query rewriting
presentation.summary: Rewrites a Snowflake query for performance without changing its results.
benefits: Separates transformations that are safe from ones that only look safe
Explains why each rewrite preserves the result set
Keeps null and duplicate semantics intact through the rewrite

presentation.name: Technical writing
presentation.summary: Improves technical prose without changing its meaning or terminology.
benefits: Removes padding and boilerplate that add length but no information
Preserves defined terms and technical claims exactly as written
Replaces unnatural phrasing with how an engineer would actually say it
Flags sentences whose meaning is unclear instead of guessing at them

presentation.name: Test design and review
presentation.summary: Decides what is worth testing and judges whether existing tests would catch a defect.
benefits: Derives cases from behaviour and boundaries rather than from code shape
Identifies tests that pass regardless of whether the code is correct
Covers failure paths, not only the successful one
Distinguishes untested code from code that cannot be tested as written

presentation.name: Work verification
presentation.summary: Checks that work actually does what was asked before it is reported as finished.
benefits: Requires observed command output before any claim that something passes
Separates passed, failed, skipped and never-run instead of merging them
Checks the original request was met, not only that the code runs
Reports what was not verified rather than leaving it implied
